measurements.name: cpcb-aqi-exceedance
measurements.built_from: one pinned XKDR export of the CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 stream (data.xkdr.org)

export_pin.note: asserted by the build through /v1/meta; a changed or re-exported source refuses the build

measurements.grain: one row per complete (n_hours >= 18) cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 station-day D with a labelable D+1 (a row present with n_hours >= 18), at the 23:59 IST instant of day D

population.eligibility: scored rows are complete (n_hours >= 18) station-days of the cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 stream with day D inside the declared window AND a labelable D+1 (a row present with n_hours >= 18). Day-D completeness is knowable at the instant; the D+1 observability rule is an outcome-observability exclusion that never reads the label value - unlabelable rows are excluded and counted per split. The 2025-04..09 partial tail (47,566 station-days, 829 valid-day positives) is excluded and counted; the 2025-01..03 and 2025-10..12 hole months are asserted empty. Both label values are retained in every window
population.identity: station_day = <station_id>|<date>, unique across the panel (asserted at construction)
population.censoring: excluded and counted per split: thin day D (n_hours < 18) @@THIN@@; unlabelable D+1 @@UNLAB@@; outside the declared windows @@OUTSIDE@@; the 2025-04..09 partial tail @@TAIL@@ station-days (@@TAILPOS@@ valid-day positives) excluded and counted; the 2025-01..03 and 2025-10..12 hole months are asserted empty (0 rows)

label.definition: the station's D+1 calendar-day 24-hour mean PM2.5 exceeds 90 ug/m3 (strict >), the Poor-band lower breakpoint of CPCB's National AQI for 24-hour PM2.5; both the D and D+1 days must carry n_hours >= 18
label.threshold_source: https://cpcb.gov.in/upload/Downloads/AQI_Bulletin_20241118.pdf (retained probe/out/aqi_bulletin_20241118.pdf); the 90 ug/m3 edge is the Poor-band lower breakpoint of CPCB's own National AQI (About AQI PDF, probe/out/about_aqi.pdf, corroborated by AQI-Calculator.xlsx). Measured panel confirmation: 36/36 complete Delhi cpcb station-days on 2024-11-18 carry a 24-hr mean > 90 ug/m3 (235.7-731.5)

runner_contract_probe.agreement_note: report.py's 1e-9 'agreement' flag prints false only because validate.py logs 4 decimals; the two AUCs agree to ~2e-6. Recorded as a reporting defect in the candidate record, not ignored.

references.measured_on: the identical 126,570 eval rows (2023), post-acceptance, every rate table estimated from train (2019-2022) only; the holdout was never opened
references.deciding_rule: headroom is demonstrated ONLY if the full model beats EVERY member of (station_persistence, state_season_climatology, global_rate) with a station-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero in the model's favour AND the model's own cluster-bootstrap AUC CI lies entirely above 0.5 (degenerate constant member); triad dominance -> recorded defect (drop or re-target); no re-tuning of threshold, window, label or features after any score

station_persistence.definition: the station's most recent observed daily value: the shipped pm25_mean of day D scored directly as the probability-like ranking for D+1 exceedance (full coverage by construction - every scored row carries a complete day D)

state_season_climatology.definition: train-estimated exceedance rate per (state_name x season of the TARGET day D+1); the state's train rate then the global train rate are the fallbacks

global_rate.definition: constant train exceedance rate; no ranking information, AUC degenerate by construction

station_train_rate.definition: supplementary identity prior: train-estimated exceedance rate per station_id, global rate as fallback (reported, never a deciding member)

majority_class.definition: majority label fitted on train, measured against this split's labels

deciding_check.rule: headroom is demonstrated ONLY if the full model beats EVERY triad member with a station-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero in the model's favour; triad dominance -> recorded defect, drop or re-target; no re-tuning after any score

model_minus_member_ci.note: cluster-aware paired bootstrap on identical eval rows, clusters = station_id; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity
cluster-aware paired bootstrap on identical eval rows, clusters = station_id; an interval containing zero is inconclusive, not parity

global_rate.treatment: constant member, no ranking information; beaten iff the model's cluster-bootstrap AUC CI lies entirely above 0.5

model_auc_ci.note: one-sample cluster-aware bootstrap of AUC, clusters = station_id

comparison.verdict_scope: eval split only (2023 station-days); prevalence and the seasonal structure are reported beside the number; the sealed holdout (2024) was not evaluated and no holdout figure exists or is implied
comparison.interpretation: the model beats every pre-registered member with the station-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero, so headroom IS demonstrated under the rule written before any score. The label is largely persistence-carried: the model's edge over persistence is real but small (+@@GAPFULL@@ AUC), and persistence itself dominates climatology by +0.1073 [@@CI_PC@@]. No figure may be quoted without the comparison.

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one station-day next-day exceedance prediction at 23:59 IST on day D; features are precomputed at construction and the runner predicts row-wise from the shipped columns. Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: XKDR publishes a single cleaned export (no historical vintages, no first-publication ledger), so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed - retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

vintage.evidence: the archive is one export stamped 2026-09-30T11:25:11+00:00 (/v1/meta, asserted by this build: exported_at and the 196,521,834-row count are pinned; a re-export refuses the build). Values are 'as reported' with 'no gap filling' and marked 'preliminary and not fully validated' (XKDR README); revision behaviour is unmeasured because a second export has never been observed. Every shipped feature is the current-vintage value of a measurement at or before day D; no as-of value is claimed

selection.evidence: membership is fixed by day-D completeness (n_hours >= 18, knowable at the instant) and the declared window; the only additional rule is D+1 outcome observability (a row with n_hours >= 18 must exist for D+1), which never reads the label value - unlabelable rows are excluded and counted per split. Positives are winter-clustered, so the day-level observability rule could in principle co-move with the label through weather (a monsoon D+1 is both thin and clean); the excluded counts per split and per month are recorded in summary.json so the exclusion's seasonality is measurable, not hidden

measurements.prevalence_shift: positive rate declines across the temporal split (21.15% train 2019-2022 -> 15.66% eval 2023 -> 12.56% holdout 2024): an out-of-distribution as well as temporal test; recorded as a property, not repaired
measurements.seasonality: positives are winter-clustered (eval 2023: DJF @@DJF@@ vs JJAS @@JJAS@@ prevalence); every interval in the deciding check is station-clustered (cluster = station_id, @@EVALCLUSTERS@@ eval clusters)

data_compilation.scope: Our contribution - the station-day eligibility frame (complete cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 station-days, n_hours >= 18, with a labelable D+1), the derived binary next-day exceedance label (calendar-day D+1 24-hr mean PM2.5 > 90 ug/m3, the CPCB National AQI Poor-band lower breakpoint), the at-instant trailing-history feature derivations and calendar fields, the sentinel handling for stations with no state_name, the excluded-and-counted thin/unlabelable/outside-window accounting, and the temporal partition (train 2019-2022 / eval 2023 / holdout 2024) - is dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. The dedication covers only our contribution: the underlying CPCB CAAQM measurements and the XKDR compilation keep their own designations and remain subject to GODL-India and CC BY 4.0 respectively, whose attribution requirements carry through to every copy of the derived data. Nothing here relicenses the source or presents CC0 as the source's terms.

source_data.status: Two preserved upstream instruments, neither relicensed. CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 measurements: Government Open Data License - India (GODL-India v1.0) via the data.gov.in platform instrument, with its attribution template, non-endorsement, no-warranty and continuity conditions. The XKDR Forum Air-Quality-Database compilation carrying those measurements: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with the README's own requested credit. The redistributed fields are the publisher's own station identifiers, timestamps and hourly PM2.5 measurements (aggregated by us to daily statistics) plus our derived label, features and partition. The derived dataset is labelled as such throughout and is neither a CPCB product nor an XKDR Forum product.

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.
